A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NPNet research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite expanded and rearranged supplementary material in v5.

before.justification: v4 reports original NPNet evaluations, ablations, sampler and seed-range experiments, FID measurements and generated-image comparisons.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results and adds compositional evaluation, few-step model experiments, distribution analyses and method-combination results.

M1.justification: The re-denoise sampling, preference filtering, two-branch NPNet, training objective and inference procedure remain in Equations 5–9 and Algorithms 1–3. The new architecture and batch-prompt descriptions disclose implementation details without establishing a revision to the underlying method.

E1.justification: v5 adds T2I-CompBench test prompts covering attribute binding, spatial and non-spatial relationships, numeracy and complex composition. This extends the existing compositional text-to-image coverage while retaining Pick-a-Pic, DrawBench, HPD v2, GenEval and ImageNet evaluation. The added few-step models reuse GenEval.

E2.justification: Table 20 adds comparisons of PAG, CFG++, APG, FreeU, SAG and SEG with and without NPNet. Repaint is removed from Table 2 and several corresponding plots and qualitative comparisons, although its non-MPS aggregate scores reappear as Re-sampling in Table 20. The earlier DPO, AYS and InitNO experiments remain.

E3.justification: v5 adds direct compositional GenEval scoring alongside the retained preference-score evaluation, plus T2I-CompBench metrics. New protocols evaluate LCM and SDXL-Lightning at four steps and PCM at eight steps, examine 100 noises per prompt in Figure 9, and compare 50 generated images against ImageNet in Figure 13. Existing training budgets and main test subsets remain.

E4.justification: New analyses examine prompt-specific noise-residual clustering, generated-image distribution density, transfer to few-step models and compatibility with seven noise-optimization methods. Figures 24–33 also add qualitative cases. The earlier architecture, filtering, hyperparameter, sampler and seed-range analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The seed-range experiment is retained without a new repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice. Neither version reports confidence intervals or formal significance tests. v5's description of distribution alignment as statistically significant is not accompanied by a reported test.

E6.justification: New Tables 8, 14, 18 and 20 substantially expand reported outcomes. In the new GenEval Table 14, standard versus NPNet overall scores are 51.58 versus 53.49, while Colors falls from 85.11 to 82.98. Most matched table values persist; Table 2's CLIPScore conversion from percentages to decimals is equivalent. Some Repaint entries disappear, and qualitative examples and efficiency plot points change.

T1.justification: Theorem E.1, its assumptions, Taylor-expansion derivation and Equations 10–14 are unchanged after accounting for intervening tables and pagination. The principal mathematical definitions and method equations are also retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: noise prompt learning, the NPD/NPNet framework, and efficient improvement across diffusion models. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the core contribution or novelty claim.

C2.justification: v5 interprets residual clustering as evidence of semantic information and the density visualization as movement toward real-data high-density regions. It also introduces batch-prompt sharing as a possible regularizer and adds a claim that seed generalization preserves diversity. Appendix F's limitations and future directions remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.4 and Figure 11 disclose the Swin-Tiny backbone, 224-by-224 resizing, channel projections, MLP branches, skip connections and SVD-branch code. Appendix A.5 newly describes assigning one prompt across a batch, and A.2 adds a CLIPScore implementation reference. These substantially expand implementation documentation without establishing that experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v5 adds references concerning prompt corruption, One More Step, T2I-CompBench, few-step diffusion and additional guidance methods, with limited accompanying discussion. The existing related-work narrative and positioning as the first noise-prompt learning framework remain.

P1.justification: v5 adds architecture, density-analysis and visualization subsections, targeted explanatory paragraphs and acknowledgements. The author and affiliation block changes. Most main-text wording and the overall section sequence remain, so this is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v5 adds compositional and combination tables, clustering and density plots, an implementation snapshot and ten qualitative galleries. It redraws Figure 2, removes Repaint series from several plots, reorganizes the earlier Figure 18 into Figure 23, and resizes or relocates retained displays. These are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v5 provides more direct evidence for compositional performance, broader compatibility testing and substantially clearer implementation details. These improve support and reproducibility. The benefit is tempered by overinterpretation: Table 14 shows declining color accuracy despite the surrounding claim of universally improved metrics, and the new density visualization is described as statistically significant without a test. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
